coverage.limits: Index coverage is not complete coverage of runtime effects, procedural cooking, mods, translated aliases, gas density or all tonic interactions.

acute blinking tic.note: Unplanned teleportation can invalidate the route; reassess the resulting position.

asleep.note: Cannot act; reduced defense makes incoming attacks dangerous. Waking may leave dazed.

berserk.note: Improves axe dismemberment; does not establish general safety.

blaze tonic.note: Heat protection comes with cold vulnerability and a need to move; stationary waiting can ignite the user.

bleeding.note: Ongoing HP loss; use a survival plan and verify bleeding ends.

blind.note: Sight is impaired; do not infer an empty area from missing visible enemies.

blurry vision.note: Visual information is degraded; rely on public descriptions and re-observe.

broken.note: The affected object cannot be used or equipped; review replacement or repair.

budding.note: A clone is pending; recuperation can cancel the effect.

burning.note: Ongoing fire damage; verify native firefighting outcome rather than assuming waiting extinguishes it.

choking on ash.note: Ash exposure causes ongoing damage; leave exposure and verify recovery.

cleaved.note: Armor value is reduced; reassess incoming physical damage.

coated in plasma.note: Heat/cold/electric resistance drops; temperature cannot normalize passively and firefighting is weakened.

confused.note: Names and map glyphs can be scrambled and defenses reduced; preserve prior observations, verify actual action results.

corrected vision.note: Vision correction is beneficial; other conditions still apply.

covered in liquid.note: Resolve the liquid and exposure route; coating alone does not establish disease or ingestion.

covered in spores.note: This named effect causes ongoing damage; distinguish it from fungal infection onset.

cracked.note: Armor value is reduced; reassess incoming physical damage.

dazed.note: Agility, intelligence and movement are impaired.

deep dreaming.note: Unresponsive; the dream context requires upper-level interpretation.

disoriented.note: Dodge and mental defenses are reduced.

emboldened.note: Temporary HP benefit; do not treat temporary maximum HP as permanent growth.

enclosed.note: Exit costs a turn and may fail or hurt; read the enclosing object's actual effect description.

exhaustion.note: Cannot take actions; danger increases when enemies or damage overlap.

flying.note: Changes melee reach and terrain exposure; do not assume flight can never fail.

frenzied.note: Quickness improves but aggression changes; retain current tactical intent.

frozen.note: Physical actions are blocked; verify warming and escape in the next observation.

gleaming.note: Visible special effect; inspect its public description without inferring immunity.

glotrot.note: Eating/drinking can cause bleeding; lost speech can block quests. Cure recipe is generated per game; regrowth alone is insufficient.

greased.note: Helps traverse webs; does not grant universal immunity to liquid or terrain hazards.

grounded.note: Flight is unavailable; do not rely on airborne protection.

hobbled.note: Movement is greatly slowed; reassess escape margins.

hyper-responsive.note: Temporary quickness increase is followed by sluggishness; consider the transition.

ill.note: Natural HP regeneration stops and healing is reduced; ordinary resting is not a recovery plan.

inspired.note: Affects future cooking choices; no immediate injury is implied.

interdicted.note: Movement is slowed; account for pursuit.

ironshank.note: Progressive movement loss can outweigh its AV gain; plan the game-specific cure.

itchy skin.note: Fungal infection onset needs timely planning; ordinary disease remedies do not necessarily work.

latched onto.note: Break free before moving; verify whether escape succeeded.

lost.note: World-map fast travel is unavailable until orientation is recovered.

lovesick.note: Mental attributes and movement are reduced.

metabolizing.note: Cooking effects are procedural; use the full public description, never assume every meal is safe.

monochrome.note: Color information is limited; do not classify danger from color alone.

mutating.note: Delayed mutation can add a defect and alter the build; request an upper-level plan.

omniphase.note: Can interact across phases; ordinary phasing protection is not universal.

overburdened.note: Cannot move until the burden is addressed; do not repeat movement commands.

paralyzed.note: Movement and attacks are blocked and dodge is lost.

phase spider venom.note: Damage, reduced healing and phasing overlap; verify interaction and exit position before phase ends.

phased.note: Interaction requires compatible phase; materializing completely inside solid terrain can be fatal.

phosphorescent.note: Emits light; does not establish enemy absence or other immunity.

poisoned.note: Ongoing damage blocks natural regeneration and reduces healing; illness may follow.

poisoned by gas.note: Gas poison causes ongoing damage; do not automatically import venom's recovery penalties.

power skating.note: Faster movement trades off melee accuracy and possibly dodge; review before fighting.

prone.note: Standing costs a turn; reduced defenses and contact with floor liquids can compound danger.

proselytized.note: Recruitment changes allegiance; infer neither bodily damage nor hostility from this effect alone.

psionically cleaved.note: Mental armor is reduced; mental attacks become more dangerous.

pulsed.note: EMP-sensitive devices or robotic bodies can stop working; inspect the affected subject.

rusted.note: Metal gear may become unusable and a repeated rust event can destroy it; robotic bodies can also be slowed.

shaken.note: Dodge is reduced; consider hostile proximity.

shamed.note: Multiple combat and mental penalties reduce safety margins.

shimmering.note: Severe quickness reduction changes action timing despite the perceptual benefit.

sitting.note: Standing takes a turn and dodge is reduced; the chair may heal or damage, so read its description.

sluggish.note: Quickness is reduced; allow for enemies acting more often.

sore throat.note: Possible glotrot onset; plan prevention or the current game's cure before speech is lost.

springing.note: Improves sprint/power-skating speed; does not remove their attack tradeoffs.

sprinting.note: Faster travel can reduce defense/accuracy; attacking or other actions may end it.

stained by liquid.note: A dry stain is not current liquid contact; do not infer ongoing damage from its name.

stiff legs.note: Possible ironshank onset; plan prevention before mobility progressively worsens.

stony.note: Movement penalty grows each turn; safe recuperation can remove this particular effect.

stuck.note: Movement is blocked; verify attempts to break free.

stunned by gas.note: Gas density controls slowing versus complete inaction; density may be unobserved.

submerged.note: Underwater position changes interactions; do not infer immunity to the liquid.

syphoned.note: Life is drained over time; reassess the source and continuing exposure.

terrified.note: Forced fleeing can override intended actions; recheck position and surroundings.

wakeful.note: Temporarily prevents sleep; other impairments remain possible.

waking dream.note: Dream progression changes the objective and consequences; request contextual planning.

healing.note: Publicly observed gradual HP recovery; it does not erase confusion, poison or illness.

blinded.note: Sight is impaired; do not infer an empty area from missing visible enemies.

webbed.note: Movement is blocked; verify attempts to break free.

entangled.note: Movement is blocked; verify attempts to break free.

grabbed.note: Break free before moving; verify whether escape succeeded.

nosebleed.note: Ongoing HP loss; use a survival plan and verify bleeding ends.

liquids.name: acid
liquids.note: Current contact can injure the body and equipment; resistance of one does not prove safety of the other.

liquids.name: algae
liquids.note: Coating alone is not disease or poisoning.

liquids.name: asphalt
liquids.note: Ground contact can hinder movement; burning liquid and ingestion are separate risks.

liquids.name: black ooze
liquids.note: Ingestion, prone contact or miasma can cause disease; coating alone is not a diagnosis.

liquids.name: blood
liquids.note: External blood is not evidence of active bleeding.

liquids.name: brain brine
liquids.note: Ingestion can confuse and change mental/build properties; a stain is not ingestion.

liquids.name: brown sludge
liquids.note: Prone exposure can rust gear; confirm actual rust rather than inferring it from coating.

liquids.name: cider
liquids.note: Ingestion and coating differ; consumption can cause confusion.

liquids.name: cloning draught
liquids.note: Pure exposure may initiate cloning; mixed-liquid purity is not known from the adjective alone.

liquids.name: convalessence
liquids.note: Ground contact cools and can heal organic creatures; watch freezing instead of treating it as unconditionally safe.

liquids.name: gel
liquids.note: Open liquid terrain may cause slipping; dry stains do not.

liquids.name: green goo
liquids.note: Prone contact or ingestion may poison; watch for the actual effect.

liquids.name: honey
liquids.note: Open terrain may trap movement; carried food or a stain is a different exposure.

liquids.name: ink
liquids.note: Open terrain can cause sliding; wiki depth formulas vary by version and are not used here.

liquids.name: lava
liquids.note: Dangerous heat exposure; verify both body and equipment condition.

liquids.name: molten wax
liquids.note: Sticky terrain; the word molten alone does not justify applying the lava rule.

liquids.name: neutron flux
liquids.note: Open/contact flux is an extreme hazard. A safely contained phial is not current bodily exposure; containment failure is separate.

liquids.name: oil
liquids.note: Slippery terrain and combustible liquid; coating does not prove an extra fire-damage multiplier.

liquids.name: primordial soup
liquids.note: Mixed open pools can generate hostile sludge; composition and volume are not inferred from appearance alone.

liquids.name: putrescence
liquids.note: Drinking can cause vomiting and water loss; coating alone is not that event.

liquids.name: salt
liquids.note: Do not substitute salty liquid for safe drinking water; a dry crust is not thirst damage.

liquids.name: sap
liquids.note: Open terrain may impede movement.

liquids.name: slime
liquids.note: Terrain can cause slipping; ingestion can confuse; coating alone proves neither.

liquids.name: sunslag
liquids.note: Consumption can improve quickness; external coating is not a stat gain.

liquids.name: warm static
liquids.note: Impure contact can produce arbitrary effects; pure pouring/drinking can transform a body or build. Do not assume purity.

liquids.name: water
liquids.note: Liquid water, frozen terrain and scalding vapor differ; observe the actual condition.

liquids.name: wine
liquids.note: Ingestion may confuse; a coating or stain is not intoxication.

tonics.name: blaze injector
tonics.note: Heat protection and quickness trade off cold resistance; non-movement heats the user and burning ends the tonic. Adverse reaction can ignite.

tonics.name: eaters' nectar injector
tonics.note: Permanent build change differs by genotype. The wiki identifies this tonic as exempt from overdose; do not apply generic overdose rules to it.

tonics.name: hulk honey injector
tonics.note: Strength and temporary HP trade off movement and ongoing nonlethal self-damage. Pain suppression hides exact HP in ordinary play; do not rely on apparently precise bridge HP. Adverse reaction can cause enraged confusion.

tonics.name: love injector
tonics.note: Allegiance/affection changes are contextual; adverse reaction can ignite the user.

tonics.name: rubbergum injector
tonics.note: Elemental/bludgeoning protection trades off AV and bleeding saves; adverse reaction can repeatedly cause prone unless flying.

tonics.name: salve injector
tonics.note: Healing is gradual and reduced by poison/illness. Ordinary adverse reactions can reduce the benefit; Tonic Allergy can cause a random adverse effect while retaining healing.

tonics.name: shade oil injector
tonics.note: Mutants can phase randomly; verify phase-compatible actions and safe materialization. Adverse reaction can spawn hostile shadow clones.

tonics.name: skulk injector
tonics.note: Benefits differ between darkness and daylight; light-based damage is amplified. Adverse reaction can cause blindness.

tonics.name: sphynx salt injector
tonics.note: Confusion protection and genotype-specific benefits; adverse reaction can impose long mental-mutation cooldowns. Precognition is not an available executor action.

tonics.name: ubernostrum injector
tonics.note: Gradual healing and delayed biological-debuff removal/limb regrowth; do not assume an immediate universal cure. Tonic Allergy can cause random adverse effects.

tonics.name: luminous hoarshroom
tonics.note: This food counts as a tonic. Healing ends before its other benefits; poison prevention does not cure existing poison. Adverse reaction freezes and 100 cold resistance does not fully prevent it.
